item.title: Emancipation or Instrumentalisation in Erasmus+ Mobility: A Literature Review

item.title: The Importance of the School Magazine as an Extra-Curricular Activity in Facilitating Students’ Cross-Curricular Skills and Competences
item.description: The paper discusses the school magazine as an important extracurricular activity. We first define the characteristics of school magazines, pointing to aims, content focus, types of texts and the organisation of editorial boards. item.title: Video Games and the Development of Computational Thinking
item.description: For many, video games represent a popular form of entertainment. However, numerous research studies confirm that playing video games is a complex process with a significant educational component in addition to entertainment. Several researchers, including Papert and other authorities, have argued that we can learn a great deal about the learning process through video games, either by playing them ourselves or by observing others play and discussing the processes and thinking strategies involved.

item.description: Two global trends that can be observed in computing education all over the world are moving the beginning of teaching computing as a compulsory school subject to primary education and moving from the teaching of user approaches to digital technologies to computer science content. item.title: Developing Digital Literacy in Pre-Service Primary School Teachers Through a Massive Open Online Course and Project-Based Learning
item.description: The present paper examines the implementation of a massive open online course and project-based learning to develop the digital competences of preservice teachers. The course design was based on the Digital Competence Framework for Citizens. item.title: The Factors Influencing the Process of Deciding Whether to Become a Computer Science Teacher
item.description: Choosing a future profession is an important step in life, and the decision to become a teacher is widely discussed in the literature.
